INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS WHO Global TB Report 2026: India Records 38% Decline in TB Mortality and 94% Treatment Success Rate In November 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) released its ‘Global Tuberculosis Report 2026’ highlighting that India achieved a 38% decline in tuberculosis (TB) mortality between 2015 and 2025, surpassing the global reduction of 35%, and recorded a 94% treatment success rate for drug-susceptible TB. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 ✓ By Whom? WHO ✓ India record: 38% reduction in TB mortality between 2015 and 2025 surpassing reduction of 35% ✓ Implementing Programme: NTEP ✓ India’s Campaign: TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan ✓ TB Screening Coverage: Over 25 crore people ✓ TB Cases Detected: 48.64 lakh. About WHO Global TB Report 2026: Overview: The report provides an assessment of the global TB epidemic and progress in prevention, diagnosis and treatment, based on data from 187 countries and areas, representing more than 99% of the world’s population and TB cases. Global TB Burden: In 2025, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB, while 1.13 million people died from the disease. Burden: In 2025, eight countries accounted for approximately 67% of global TB cases, led by India (25%), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%). WHO Recognition: The WHO South-East Asia Regional Office (WHO SEARO) acknowledged India’s contribution to reducing TB mortality across the region. India’s Progress: TB Progress: India reduced its estimated TB mortality rate from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 in 2025, while meeting around 96% of its TB programme funding requirements through domestic resources, demonstrating sustained national investment in TB elimination. Programme: The Pradhan Mantri (PM) TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan(2022), implemented under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), under Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), strengthens proactive screening, early diagnosis and community outreach, particularly among vulnerable and high-risk populations. • Campaign: The first 100-day campaign began on 7 December 2024 in 347 districts across 33 States and Union Territories (UTs), followed by a second campaign on 24 March 2026, targeting 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings and vulnerable populations. Screening: Between 7 December 2024 and 8 November 2026, the campaign screened over 25 crore individuals, conducted 11 crore chest X-rays and 3 crore Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAAT), and detected 48.64 lakh new TB cases, including 14.97 lakh asymptomatic cases.
